answer_text:
We need to evaluate

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1+\frac12+\cdots+\frac1n}{(\pi^n+e^n)^{1/n}\ln n}.
\]

Let

\[
H_n=1+\frac12+\cdots+\frac1n
\]

be the \(n\)-th harmonic number. It is well known that

\[
H_n=\ln n+\gamma+o(1),
\]

so in particular

\[
\frac{H_n}{\ln n}\to 1.
\]

Now consider the other factor:

\[
(\pi^n+e^n)^{1/n}.
\]

Since \(\pi>e\), we can factor out \(\pi^n\):

\[
(\pi^n+e^n)^{1/n}
= \left(\pi^n\left(1+\left(\frac{e}{\pi}\right)^n\right)\right)^{1/n}
= \pi\left(1+\left(\frac{e}{\pi}\right)^n\right)^{1/n}.
\]

Because \(\frac{e}{\pi}<1\),

\[
\left(\frac{e}{\pi}\right)^n\to 0.
\]

Hence

\[
\left(1+\left(\frac{e}{\pi}\right)^n\right)^{1/n}\to 1,
\]

so

\[
(\pi^n+e^n)^{1/n}\to \pi.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\frac{1+\frac12+\cdots+\frac1n}{(\pi^n+e^n)^{1/n}\ln n}
=
\frac{H_n}{\ln n}\cdot \frac{1}{(\pi^n+e^n)^{1/n}}
\to 1\cdot \frac1\pi.
\]

Thus the limit is

\[
\boxed{\frac{1}{\pi}}.
\]

27B·v4.method: Identify H_n ~ ln n and (π^n+e^n)^(1/n) → π, then the ratio simplifies to (H_n/ln n)/A_n → 1/π.
